data.note:
Reflection: I called Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.66) but truth is Protein degradation for proteasome inhibitor I (CID 16760625, no curated ChEMBL mechanism).

Why I missed: all 4 wells showed strong tubulin brightening (tub_mean z +4.8 to +11.3, tub_glcm_contrast z +30 at 10uM) with enlarged/spread cells, and two independent microscopist reads both called stabilization/bundling with multinucleation. Proteasome blockade can alter tubulin turnover/proteostasis and produce stabilization-like brightness, which the vision model misread.

Literature check: PSI used as proteasome inhibitor e.g. PMID:11433385, PMID:18468579; tubulin stability-proteostasis link e.g. PMID:37435044.

Lesson: strong single-stain change is not class-specific; should have kept Protein degradation on board given nuclear enlargement + cell loss pattern and low-similarity atlas, and requested proteasome functional assay as follow-up.

reflection.text:
I concluded microtubule stabilizers at p=0.66 after seeing sustained tubulin brightening across 0.3-10 uM and two microscopist stabilizer calls, but unblinding showed proteasome inhibitor I whose true class is protein degradation. The quantitative atlas never supported my call: NSC votes were split Aurora 1/2 then DNA damage 2/4 with low similarities 0.289-0.36 and k-neighbours split across Aurora, DNA damage, DNA replication and protein synthesis.

What misled me was the measurement tub_mean z=+7.6 to +11.3 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 at 10 uM, which I read as direct stabilization, reinforced by the comparison choice to discount the weak split NSC as noisy and the acquisition choice to sample only four mid-to-high dose wells with no low-dose onset, no proteasome reference, and no functional read. I left protein degradation at 0.01 throughout and never tested it, even though nuclear eccentricity, reduced nuc_dna_mean with increased integrated DNA, and cell loss rho=-0.80 were compatible with proteotoxic/mitotic stress rather than pure stabilization.

The lesson is that tubulin intensity alone does not distinguish stabilizers from proteostasis-mediated tubulin accumulation, and visual calls cannot outweigh a consistently non-stabilizer atlas without a polymerization or ubiquitin assay to break the tie.
what_was_right: Detected a potent phenotype: strong tubulin intensity/texture signal plus dose-related cell loss rho=-0.80 and nuclear eccentricity/DNA shifts across 4 wells.
Recognized atlas evidence was weak and split with low per-well similarities 0.289-0.36 and no stabilizer vote, and flagged uncertainty in the rationale.
Noted mitotic/nuclear abnormalities and lower density that were in fact compatible with proteotoxic stress, even if assigned to the wrong upstream cause.
what_was_wrong: Misinterpreted measurement tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast elevation as direct microtubule stabilization, missing secondary tubulin accumulation from proteasome blockade.

Over-weighted comparison to two microscopist stabilizer calls and dose-response rho=+0.80 for tub_mean while dismissing NSC DNA damage 2/4 and Aurora/protein synthesis votes that correctly excluded stabilizers.

Acquisition choice sampled only 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with no low-dose, no control compounds, and no ubiquitin/proteasome or polymerization assay, and kept protein degradation hypothesis at 0.01 without testing.

citations.claim: PSI is documented as a proteasome inhibitor, supporting protein degradation as the true MOA for this compound.
PSI treatment induces broad proteome changes in HL-60 cells consistent with blockade of protein degradation.
Disrupted proteostasis can compromise tubulin stability, providing a plausible route for proteasome inhibition to mimic a tubulin-bright stabilizer phenotype.

reflection.next_experiment: Compare test compound head-to-head with a reference microtubule stabilizer and a reference proteasome inhibitor: proteasome activity plus ubiquitinated-protein accumulation assay, and in vitro tubulin polymerization plus washout immunofluorescence for true bundled microtubules versus secondary tubulin brightening.

- Over-weighted comparison to two microscopist stabilizer calls and dose-response rho=+0.80 for tub_mean while dismissing NSC DNA damage 2/4 and Aurora/protein synthesis votes that correctly excluded stabilizers.
- Acquisition choice sampled only 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with no low-dose, no control compounds, and no ubiquitin/proteasome or polymerization assay, and kept protein degradation hypothesis at 0.01 without testing.

Proposed next experiment: Compare test compound head-to-head with a reference microtubule stabilizer and a reference proteasome inhibitor: proteasome activity plus ubiquitinated-protein accumulation assay, and in vitro tubulin polymerization plus washout immunofluorescence for true bundled microtubules versus secondary tubulin brightening.
